correctness.rationale: Complete proof partitions all exponent patterns with \(\Omega(n)\le4\). Squarefree products have strictly positive gap, nonsingleton prime powers strictly negative; \(p^2q\) gives 12,18, \(p^3q\) impossible by q<2, \(p^2q^2\) strictly negative, \(p^2qr\) has an odd-mod-2 obstruction unless p=2, when (q-3)(r-3)=16 has unique valid distinct-prime pair (5,11). Direct substitution and independent SPF/aliquot verifier corroborate the boundary. All n>=2 quantifiers and n=1 exclusion stated; n=396 shows larger Omega need separate work.

originality.rationale: The exact defining sequences OEIS A211991 and A212127 record numerical equality cases but neither inspected entry states or proves the all-integers classification under \(\Omega(n)\le4\). The first relevant original full paper inspected, Ufnarovski–Åhlander (2003), develops D(n) but does not state an aliquot equality classification. Published nearby arithmetic-derivative cototient work concerns \(D(n)-(n-\varphi(n))\), not \(D(n)-(\\(\sigma(n)-n\))\); its results neither imply nor subsume the present theorem. Searches and statement comparisons support originality relative to inspected sources, not absolute publication priority.
residual_risks: A prior but unindexed proof of the same low-multiplicity classification could exist.
The semantic search of published records is not a certificate of uniqueness or priority; cited pages were directly compared as far as accessible.

value.rationale: The pre-existing exact equality sequence A212127 has many prime witnesses and sporadic composites. The theorem gives its first complete unrestricted prime-factor-multiplicity strata including the first three-distinct-prime witness 220. It distinguishes a finite table of examples from an all-size exclusion in every pattern up to Omega=4; 396 at Omega=5 shows a genuine new regime beyond the boundary. This is a mathematically natural classification, not a small numerical cutoff or a recomputation of existing entries.
